transcript:
This message comes from Angie. Angie has been helping homeowners find skilled pros
to get their home projects done well for over 30 years. For everything from minor repairs
to major remodels, find reviews, pricing, and booking at Angie.com or on the Angie app.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh. The Trump administration's promoting an artificial
intelligence-powered website, america.gov, that it says can swiftly provide users with information
in government services. It's being rolled out in the climate of mounting public skepticism about
AI safety and the dangers of AI developing too quickly for humans to keep up. Some AI tech giants
recently advised a slowdown in AI development, a notion President Trump has strongly rejected. He
says the US needs to stay ahead of the competition. The FBI says authorities in the Netherlands have
arrested a suspected leader of the notorious cyber criminal group that recently claimed to have hacked
an FBI computer system. Dutch national police took the individual into custody this morning.
We have more from NPR's Ryan Lucas. The FBI says the suspect is an alleged leader of the criminal
hacking group Shiny Hunters. That's the same group that last week claimed to have hacked the FBI jobs
portal and stolen private personal data and work information on thousands of current and former FBI
employees. In a video posted on X, FBI cyber official Brett Leatherman had this message
for members of Shiny Hunters. The longer you stay in this, the more we learn about you.
You know how to find us and we know how to find you. I suggest you reach out first while the
choice is still yours. The Shiny Hunter hack of the FBI jobs portal is an embarrassing episode for
the bureau and carries potentially serious counterintelligence and safety consequences.
Ryan Lucas, NPR News, Washington. Tomorrow, the US military formally
withdraws from Iraq after more than two decades. NPR's Jana Raff reports from Baghdad the withdrawal
will also mark the end of the anti-ISIS coalition that the US has led since 2014.
At what had been the Joint Military Command Center, Iraqi workers are renovating. US officers
have operated from here since 2014 when Iraq asked the US military to return to fight the
militant group ISIS. On Wednesday, US commanders and Iraqi leaders will mark the withdrawal of US
forces 23 years after the United States invaded Iraq. It's a historical day. We are very proud
to reach this day. That's Iraqi armed forces spokesman Sabah Al-Numan. At its height,
during an eight-year-long occupation, the US had 170,000 military personnel in Iraq.
Jana Raff, NPR News, Baghdad. Consumer confidence in the US economy is the lowest it has been in
more than a decade. Dana Peterson, the chief economist of the conference board that released
a survey today says, "The Consumer Confidence Index deteriorated notably in September following
two prior months of softening." Fuel prices and inflation have pushed higher as the US war with
Iran has dragged on for seven months. This is NPR News. Oil prices are inching lower but NPR Scott
Horsley says the effect on retail energy prices has been muted so far. Oil prices have backed off
their recent peaks but remain elevated as a result of the US war with Iran. AAA says retail gasoline
prices dip two cents a gallon overnight to an average of $4.46 a gallon. Diesel prices are
averaging just under $6.44 a gallon. Higher jet fuel prices are driving up the cost of airline
tickets just as many people are booking flights for upcoming holiday travel. The cost of airline
tickets in August was up more than 23 percent from a year ago. Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
In Texas, Governor Greg Abbott has issued a statewide disaster proclamation over record
high diesel prices. Texas Public Radio's Marianne Navarro has more. Abbott said soaring diesel
prices has put Texas's agricultural and freight industries at risk. The 30-day declaration waves
dyed diesel restrictions in the state and raises the allowable weight for fuel, agricultural and
timber loads. Dyed diesel is off-road fuel marked red that is typically barred on public roadways.
The declaration also suspends Texas low emissions diesel rules to the extent authorized by the
Environmental Protection Agency. Abbott also requested that the EPA waive federal ultra-low
sulfur diesel requirements, which would allow more fuel at the pumps and could reduce prices.
I'm Marianne Navarro in San Antonio. The Premier League, the top tier of England's soccer league
system, confirms today that Manchester City's been found guilty of nearly all 100-plus charges
of financial wrongdoing. Man City has denied the allegations. You're listening to NPR News.
